title: Binding an independent product coordinatewise
statement: Let $I$ be a finite index set, and let $A_i$ and $B_i$ be finite sets for each $i\in I$. Choose a probability mass function $p_i$ on $A_i$ and, for each $a\in A_i$, a probability mass function $q_i(a)$ on $B_i$. If a tuple is first sampled from the independent product of the $p_i$ and then each coordinate $i$ is sampled from $q_i$ at its original value, the resulting distribution is the independent product of the coordinatewise distributions obtained by sampling from $p_i$ and then from $q_i$.
hypotheses_covered: a probability mass function $p_i$ on each $A_i$
a probability mass function $q_i(a)$ on each $B_i$ for every $a\in A_i$
